rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting standard for native customs
rubrics_metrics.description: The author states: 'I have never accepted an explanation of a native custom from one person alone, nor have I set down things as being prevalent customs from having seen a single instance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a reporting principle for travel/ethnographic writing, verify customs from multiple informants and avoid generalizing from a single example; treat multiple, corroborated observations as the basis for claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground claims on personal experience and careful observation
rubrics_metrics.description: The author declares: 'I have written only on things that I know from personal experience and very careful observation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel writing and ethnographic description should, where possible, be based on first-hand observation and repeated corroboration rather than hearsay; acknowledge limits of one's knowledge and geographic scope when making general statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-travel health precautions (practical advice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical medical advice reported: 'abstain from exposing yourself to the direct rays of the sun, take 4 grains of quinine every day for a fortnight before you reach the Rivers, and get some introductions to the Wesleyans.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as contemporaneous practical guidance for travellers to West Africa (late-19th-century medical practice). It should be interpreted in historical context and compared with modern medical advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packing and baggage recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical packing advice: the author bought a long waterproof sack closed at the top with a bar and handle, used for blankets, boots, books and anything not fitting in portmanteau; it proved serviceable despite initial misgivings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: choose simple, robust, waterproof baggage and test it; prioritize practicality and items repeatedly recommended by experienced residents/traders when preparing for remote travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward single-source missionary reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The author observed that missionary literature often reports how the country is 'getting on towards being what it ought to be' and is written to solicit subscriptions rather than to provide practical country information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When researching a region, balance missionary reports with trader accounts, medical maps, and direct observations; be aware of institutional bias in sources and corroborate facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of local agents/traders and introductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical social guidance: introductions to local traders or agents (the 'Agent') and to Wesleyan missionaries can be essential; the author credits traders and agents with providing hospitality, safety, and access to places otherwise inaccessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For safe and effective field travel in the region described, cultivate introductions to trusted local agents/traders and missionary contacts; social networks are important for logistics and security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency when abridging or omitting material
rubrics_metrics.description: On the abridged edition the author explains: sections were removed 'whole' and the rest left much as first stood; she states the omitted chapters explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing an abridged edition, be transparent about what has been removed and why, and avoid implying that omitted content has been silently revised; list omitted sections for readers' reference.
